findings.message: current-pm.mjs validateAdmissionRecord/remoteAdmissionStatus accepts syntactically coherent completion without the required remote proof chain. It checks remote.version, optional slots only if present, completion target/branch/commit, then marks COMPLETE when commit is ancestor of HEAD. A record can omit source publication/merge proof, integration_evidence finalization, closure/handoff-repair proof and terminal artifact identities yet release admission. This directly violates initial-observations admission-proof ('syntactically valid completion.status alone cannot release hold').
findings.resolution: validateAdmissionRecord now invokes validateRemotePublicationRecord with requireTerminal for completed records, validateAdmissionTerminalGit checks retained terminal story/handoff modes and hashes, and completion remains blocking unless the full chain and actual local ancestry pass. The separate receipt-shape weakness reported below concerns the contents of that retained chain rather than omission of the chain.

findings.message: closure/repair provider interruption is not implemented. reconcileExecutingAttempt is called only by source publish/merge. Closure executeProviderAttempt leaves thrown executing slots stuck; closure reconcile proves Git without settling the slot. Repair uses a bespoke runner that unconditionally allocates a new token whenever effect is null, overwriting an executing active token and permitting a second write; repair reconcile also never settles slots. This violates the all-stage prepared/executing/observed and read-only recovery contract. Fresh-process lost execution must remain UNKNOWN absent exact effect adoption; same-process ended+exact absence may replay the same token.
findings.resolution: Closure and repair now use the shared durable provider engine. Their public reconciliation paths settle retained executing merge effects on the same attempt, fresh-process absence remains UNKNOWN, and same-process ended plus exact absence replays the original token.

findings.message: raced closure preimage checks compare only file text/hash, not Git mode. A concurrent 100644→100755 mode change on a P/E/H path has identical committedText, is allowed as an in-scope changed path, then wrapper restores H's mode; code accepts it, overwriting the advanced-base entry despite exact-preimage requirement.
findings.resolution: Raced closure reconciliation now compares complete committed entries at M and the advanced base, then requires the wrapper entry mode and OID to equal H.

findings.message: H2 adoption compares only captureGitAnchor().protected_hash; unlike closure/completion it retains no protectedIgnoredEntries checkout proof, so worktree-local ignored protected metadata can drift between prepare/adopt without refusal.
findings.resolution: H2 preparation retains a whole-checkout proof, and adoption checks protected ignored entries, protected Git metadata and sole branch attachment before accepting H2.

findings.message: maybeSupersedeSourceAttempt changes old.disposition/superseded_by then refreshAttempt(old), but deliberately leaves slot.effect unchanged. Its effect.attempt_identity therefore points to the pre-mutation identity that no retained attempt now has. The supersession proof omits required predecessor attempt/effect identities and validateProviderSlot never checks reciprocal links/effect-to-attempt binding. After successor success old effect pointer is replaced, so old identity is not durably recoverable.
findings.resolution: Attempt identity now covers the immutable header. Supersession retains the previous effect and observed-result history, records identified prior/current observations and predecessor effect evidence, and validates reciprocal predecessor/successor links and effect-to-attempt binding.

findings.message: rebase proof sets rebaseBase=parents[0] of final rebased commit and checks only rebaseBase..mergeCommit; for legitimate multi-commit source rebase, that parent is the preceding rebased source commit, so earlier rebased commits are outside bounded-path proof. Established premerge base is retained in merge attempt observation and should anchor the whole first-parent range. Current tests use one source commit.
findings.resolution: Rebase reconciliation now anchors the complete bounded first-parent range at the retained premerge remote-base observation, derives the authorized source delta from unique source lineage and checks every intermediate commit path plus the exact final tree.

findings.message: claimCurrentPm checks remote admission before entering transact but does not repeat it inside the transaction, contrary to the approved T05B admission dispatch. A remote record can become applicable in another checkout after the precheck and before the story write, and the claim then commits without the required hold.
findings.resolution: claimCurrentPm repeats assertRemoteAdmissionClear inside the transaction immediately before reading and changing the story.

findings.message: validateRemoteEnvelope validates only provider-slot shells and retry range, while prepareRemoteClosureCheckout trusts truthy integration_evidence.finalized/finalization. It does not validate the identified finalization or its binding to the current snapshot, gates, review and verification; a malformed/rebound record can therefore enter P/E/H closure with forged finalized evidence.
findings.resolution: The shared state validator now checks identified gates, review, verification and finalization plus their snapshot and identity links before closure can proceed. The separate finding below records that exact acceptance-criterion coverage and actor separation within those linked receipts remain insufficiently validated.

findings.message: source merge interruption treats `MERGE_PENDING` as an absence state eligible for same-process replay (`mergeRemoteSource` passes `absenceStates: ['MERGE_PENDING']`). The frozen dispatch says replay requires exact provider absence and that open/queued remains pending; an open/queued PR may already retain a provider merge request, so it cannot prove no effect and must not authorize a second merge write. This needs to stay pending/read-only unless exact merge effect is adopted.
findings.resolution: Merge recovery no longer treats MERGE_PENDING as absence. It returns pending without changing the executing attempt or issuing another provider merge.

findings.message: prepareRemoteHandoff does not require an adopted story-closure E. remotePrepareArtifact assigns `parent = closure.commit`, which can be null, persists the handoff pending record, then writes H bytes. Adoption can never accept a real commit whose parent equals null, and the dirty H write then prevents preparing E, leaving the workflow wedged. The public operation should refuse before record/file mutation until E is adopted.
findings.resolution: remotePrepareArtifact now rejects handoff preparation under the record lock unless the story-closure commit is already adopted.

findings.message: prepareHandoffRepair is not resumable across its own durable-preparation/file-write boundary. It first records a prepared attempt in withRecord, writes H2 bytes afterward, but every repeated prepare rejects whenever latest exists without race_proof. A crash after record persistence and before/while writeArtifact therefore cannot apply the retained pending after-image or return its token; the accepted prepare/adopt interruption model is broken.
findings.resolution: A retained prepared H2 attempt now resumes with its original token when the owned handoff has the exact retained content image and refuses unrelated status or a third content image. Separate findings below cover mode identity and the replacement-retry generation base.

findings.message: Premerge supersession still violates the frozen qualification rules. integration.mjs:1940-1966 can supersede source publication after a successful source merge because it never checks the merge effect/proof; it also accepts PR_DRAFT, CHECKS_PENDING and CHECKS_FAILED as qualifying current observations. remoteObservation at 1928-1934 uses `result.remoteBase || observedRemoteBase(...)`, treating an explicitly null provider base like an omitted field. The dispatch requires successful merge to forbid supersession, pending/failed observations to remain read-only, and fallback only when remoteBase is absent. Add the merge-terminal veto, restrict the qualifying current states, and distinguish an absent property from a present invalid/null value before allocating a successor.
findings.resolution: maybeSupersedeSourceAttempt now vetoes when a source merge effect or proof exists, limits qualifying fresh observations to READY or exact HEAD_MISMATCH, and remoteObservation distinguishes an omitted remoteBase from an explicit null or malformed value. A separate finding below covers mergeRemoteSource failing to return its retained terminal effect before performing a fresh inspection.

findings.message: The persisted provider-attempt validator checks transition identities and previous pointers but not the required state machine. At state.mjs:103-118, an observed attempt can be changed from prepared→executing→observed to prepared→observed by removing executing, rebinding observed.previous and reidentifying that transition; stable attempt identity and effect binding still validate, so terminal admission accepts evidence without a retained executing boundary. Enforce first prepared, prepared→executing, executing→observed with the same invocation token, and executing→prepared only with an exact replay proof; also bind active token and disposition to the legal terminal state.
findings.resolution: The validator now enforces the ordered prepared/executing/observed state machine, invocation-token continuity, legal active tokens and disposition/effect relationships. The separate replay finding below records that the retained absence result is still not bound to the attempt target's expected head.

findings.message: Remote artifact interruption recovery does not require the retained clean checkout. After remote-close-prepare persists E, restore the owned story to pending.before, make an unrelated unstaged change such as src/unrelated.txt, then call remote-close-prepare with the retained hash. remotePrepareArtifact passes clean:false for pending state and applyPending checks only the owned story, so it writes E and returns the old token amid unrelated work. H2 resume has the same gap because its anchor comparison does not cover unstaged ordinary worktree changes. The contract requires exact interruption state and preservation of unrelated work. Validate the retained pending shape and generated P/E/H or H2 image, require status to contain only the owned pending paths, and on unrelated status refuse with both owned and unrelated bytes unchanged.
findings.resolution: P/E/H and H2 recovery now validate identified pending content, retained parent and protected checkout state, require ordinary index state and allow only owned pending paths before applying the retained image. Separate findings below cover the missing independent before-story/finalization link and executable-mode identity.

findings.message: Terminal publication proof remains incompletely cross-bound. state.mjs:352-359 accepts handoff_repair.proof without requiring its retained pr_number to be a positive integer equal to the effect-bound merge attempt input.prNumber. For a normal closure, state.mjs:313-323 allows state `proven` while terminal_commit differs from the provider-bound merge_commit; rebinding that proof and completion together to a later commit that preserves the story/handoff entries can release admission even though the exact provider R was different. Require the repair PR equality and require a proven normal closure terminal to equal its merge effect commit.
findings.resolution: A normal proven closure now requires terminal_commit to equal merge_commit, and the handoff-repair terminal proof requires a positive pr_number equal to the effect-bound merge attempt input.

findings.message: Normal merge and squash reconciliation still use record.integration.base I as the provider base, while rebase correctly uses the effect-bound attempt's retained remote_observation.observed_remote_base. If the remote integration branch advances from I to proved N before the provider merge, a valid merge result with ordered parents [N,C] and exact merge-tree(N,C), or a valid squash direct child of N with that bounded source composition, is rejected at reconcileRemoteSource. T05B-AC2 and remote-lifecycle-interface.md:17 require proof against the uniquely established provider base and fresh evidence at the resulting fetched M. Derive N from the merge effect's retained observation for every method, validate it as the exact proved base, and use it for parent, bounded delta and recomputed-tree checks.
findings.resolution: Merge, squash and rebase now derive N from the effect-bound merge attempt observation, require N to descend from approved I, and use N for exact parents, recomputed composition and bounded source-delta proof.

findings.message: mergeRemoteSource does not implement the fix2 terminal fast path. After a source merge effect or source proof exists, it still calls remoteObservation/provider.inspect before executeProviderAttempt returns the retained effect. A same-input completed merge therefore depends on fresh provider and Git reads and can fail when the provider is unavailable, despite already having a durable result. T05B-fix2-design.json and T05B-supersession-dispatch.md require the successful merge to veto inspection, allocation and writes while preserving the same-input proven result.

Handoff-repair replacements generate a stale BASE_COMMIT. After HANDOFF_BASE_RACE, prepareHandoffRepair correctly selects latest.race_proof.terminal_commit as the new repairBase and pending parent, but remoteArtifactGeneration still receives closureCommit=closure.terminal_commit. The public retry therefore creates H2 as a direct child of the latest N while its handoff bytes name the original closure terminal. Resume and adoption repeat the same stale generation input, and completion later refuses the result. remote-lifecycle-interface.md:31 requires each replacement H2 to use BASE_COMMIT N for its actual latest proved parent.

Remote verification-report preparation can overwrite existing project reports. architecture-state.md:216 says P adds only docs/verification/<story-id>.md and docs/checklists/verification-<story-id>.md, and remote-lifecycle-interface.md:25 retains the existing P contract. prepareRemoteVerificationReport passes those paths to materializeRemoteWrites, which accepts non-null committed before-images. When a fetched advanced M already contains either path, the public P operation replaces it instead of refusing before durable preparation.

Remote artifact generation is not independently bound to its parent or retained after adoption. validateRemoteGeneration regenerates report/closure bytes from generation.inputs.story_before supplied by the descriptor itself but never requires that story to equal the committed parent story or pending write.before, nor does it require the retained source contract/execution identity. A coherently reidentified same-contract, different-Execution descriptor can therefore resume and adopt an E that is not the legal transition from its parent. remoteAdoptArtifact then discards the generation descriptor and records only field/commit/parent/tree/writes, so terminal P/E/H proof no longer names the source proof or remote finalization that generated it. This violates remote-lifecycle-interface.md:19 and :25, which require receipts and closure preparation to remain bound to fetched M and its finalization.

Remote artifact publication does not preserve executable Git mode. materializeRemoteWrites retains expected_mode, but applyPending writes through atomic, whose replacement file is created mode 0600, and never restores the owner's executable bit. A valid 100755 story or handoff therefore becomes 100644 during E, H or H2 preparation and cannot pass adoption's exact expected-mode check. Pending recovery also compares only text, so same-text executable-mode drift on an owned path is accepted as resumable. The existing P/E/H entry contract and remote state schema explicitly support both 100644 and 100755.

Remote terminal evidence validation does not establish exact acceptance coverage or independent actors. validateRemotePublicationRecord accepts any nonempty all-PASS verification criteria without matching their IDs exactly to source.packet.acceptance, and it does not enforce that the remote reviewer and verifier differ from the builder and each other or that required panel coverage remains present. Reidentifying a same-snapshot verification with one invented PASS criterion and colliding actors still permits finalization, closure and terminal admission. T05B-AC2 and remote-lifecycle-interface.md:19 require fresh independent review and distinct complete verification bound to M.

A retained provider replay proof is not bound to the attempt target. validateRemoteProviderSlot checks that replay.absence_result is identified PR_ABSENT evidence and binds its invocation token, but does not require absence_result.expectedHead to equal attempt.input.target.expectedHead. A reidentified replay transition can therefore claim exact absence for a different head and later support a terminal provider chain. remote-lifecycle-interface.md:9 requires exact attempt inputs and result identity before same-token replay.

remoteAdmissionStatus reports the wrong terminal field before completion preparation. It selects value.remote.closure.proof.commit, but remote-closure-proof-v1 retains merge_commit and terminal_commit. A normal or stale REMOTE_CLOSURE_PROVEN record consequently returns remote_terminal_commit:null until a completion token exists, contrary to the exact remote-admission-status projection in T05B-operation-dispatch.md.

The declared npm test gate did not complete for the frozen fix2 candidate: it terminated with ETIMEDOUT at 600 seconds. Packaging validation passed, the candidate snapshot remained unchanged, and no orphan test processes remained, but a timed-out gate is not a PASS and cannot establish T05B acceptance.

summary: Reviewed the complete original T05B scope and all three acceptance criteria at frozen snapshot 009feeee3ea2fee4433de2815ca869f6a54f74b186103a95ec0c902ca29a8c9f. The eleven round-one findings are resolved in their original forms. Fix2 resolves the five fix1 residual triggers for supersession qualification, transition ordering, unrelated checkout status, terminal PR/commit crosslinks and all-method premerge N proof, with qualified remaining gaps recorded separately. Eight new source/interface findings remain: terminal merge replay still performs fresh inspection; replacement H2 uses a stale BASE_COMMIT; remote P can overwrite existing reports; artifact generation loses its independent parent/finalization binding; executable modes are not preserved; remote terminal receipt validation does not prove exact acceptance coverage or actor separation; replay absence is not bound to the attempt head; and the admission projection omits the closure terminal. The declared npm test gate also failed by ETIMEDOUT at 600 seconds, while npm run validate passed. Raw test log SHA-256 d0a17b4e7b1e4c7b005f189e6bfa9db29d739d15a17153fb89b1c7bb5137d3c0; validation log SHA-256 8b146bfab36098ddfe081ce34555566bdef41fef310ead7321bad3fa329549f0. The source and test hashes match the frozen candidate manifest, git diff --check passed, and the snapshot remained unchanged.
